question: What exact crossing angle, in degrees, is shown for the railroad tracks in Figure 8E-1?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD does not label or specify any crossing angle, in degrees, in Figure 8E-1. The figure simply depicts the tracks crossing the pathway and the sidewalk/roadway at what appears to be a right angle (perpendicular), but no numeric angle dimension is shown or stated anywhere in the figure or the accompanying text, so an "exact" degree value cannot be cited from the evidence. Support (informational): - The accompanying text explains only that "The safety of pathway and sidewalk users is enhanced when pathways and sidewalks are designed such that they do not cross the tracks at a narrow angle," without giving a specific angle value. Guidance (recommended): - For skewed crossings generally, "If the Skewed Crossing sign is used, the symbol should show the direction of the crossing (near left to far right as shown on the sign image in Figure 8B-4, or the mirror image if the track goes from far left to near right)" — again with no degree value specified. Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Figure 8E-1 with the railroad tracks drawn perpendicular to the pathway (panel A) and to the sidewalk/roadway (panel B), but with no angle dimension or degree label anywhere in the drawing. Citations: - Figure 8E-1 (p.1035) - Section 8E.02 Support §4 (p.1036) - Section 8B.22 Guidance §2 (p.1006)
